name: Caliphal court poetry in al-Andalus
summary: Under Abd al-Rahman III and al-Hakam II, Córdoba becomes the largest city in Western Europe (~250,000 inhabitants) and a centre of Arabic poetry, philology, and translation. The library of al-Hakam II reportedly holds 400,000 volumes; the muwaššaḥ strophic poetic form is invented in Iberia.

_quarry.structural_significance: Transmits a substantial portion of Greek philosophical and scientific texts (translated 9th-c. Baghdad → 10th-c. Córdoba → 12th-c. Toledo) into Latin Europe. Andalusian Hebrew and Arabic poetic forms reshape Romance vernacular poetry from troubadour Provence to Galician-Portuguese cantigas.
